### Observed differences

- A02 and A03 swapped participation one-for-one: earlier, A02 ran in all 200 traces (about 2.2 occurrences per trace, repeated in roughly 59 in 100 traces) and A03 in none; in the later window, A03 runs exactly once in every trace and A02 in none, with A03 occupying roughly the same within-trace position A02 used to hold (mean about 0.64 of the trace). [OCC001, OCC002, POS001, POS002, REL001]
- The handover after A05 changed: earlier, every observed exit of A05 went to A02; in the later window, about 97 in 100 go to A03, with about 1.5% each to A06 and A07. [DIR003]
- A03's routing mirrors A02's old routing: earlier, A02 split its observed exits between A06 (about 55 in 100) and A07 (about 45 in 100); in the later window, A03 splits them about 50/50 between A06 and A07. [DIR001, DIR002]
- The repetition loop changed carrier: earlier, A06 always led back to A02, so repetitions alternated A02→A06→A02, with A06 repeats mostly two steps apart; in the later window, A06 leads mostly to A07 (about 51 in 100) or to itself (about 48 in 100), and consecutive A06–A06 repeats (one step apart) now make up about 26 in 100 of the observed A06–A06 pairs, which did not occur earlier. [DIR004, LAG003, LAG004]
- Relations with A02 dissolved: A05 and A07, which earlier always co-occurred with A02, now appear without it in all traces; A06 co-occurred with A02 in about 59 in 100 traces earlier and now appears without A02 in about 49 in 100, with neither present in about 51 in 100. [REL002, REL003, REL004]
- New near-fixed orders around A03: A05 always precedes A03, and A03 precedes A07 in about 99 in 100 traces; earlier, A02 preceded A07 in only about 41 in 100 traces, otherwise they interleaved. [REL005, REL007, REL004]
- A06 participates somewhat less often (about 59 in 100 traces earlier vs about 49 in 100 later) and appears later within traces (median position about 0.67 → 0.8); A05 also sits slightly later (median about 0.33 → 0.5). [POS004, POS003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the control flow around A02 was restructured into a configuration centred on A03: A02, which earlier ran in every trace and repeated in about 59 in 100 of them, is no longer observed, while A03 now runs exactly once per trace; A05 hands over to A03 instead of A02, A03 routes onward to A06 or A07 much as A02 did, and the repetition that earlier alternated between A02 and A06 (A02→A06→A02) is now carried by A06 repeating itself before the trace closes with A07. [OCC001, OCC002, REL001, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, LAG003]

The screening found 21 qualifying control-flow items against roughly 0.12 expected for an unchanged process, so the volume of signals cannot be explained by random re-splits. The hypothesis rests on direct transition-level evidence (A05→A02 replaced by A05→A03; A06→A02 replaced by A06→A06 and A06→A07), an all-or-nothing participation swap across 200-trace windows, and consistent relational and distance evidence (A05 always before A03, A03 before A07 in about 99 in 100 traces, A06 self-repeats now consecutive and A06→A07 mostly one step apart). [DIR003, DIR004, REL005, REL007, LAG003, LAG004, screening]

Limitations: zero participation shows only that A02 was not observed in the later sample, and several items describe the same underlying traces rather than independent confirmations. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that A02 still executes at a very low rate outside these 200 sampled traces, which would make this a drastic routing shift away from A02 rather than its complete disappearance. [OCC001]

Other differences: the A05→A07 distance, earlier concentrated at two and four steps, now spreads across one to five steps, and the A05→A06 and A06→A07 gaps shifted toward smaller lags. These fit the restructure as downstream effects but are event-position observations, not clock-time shifts. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG004]
